newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end lower, await U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end lower, await U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Argentine stocks gave back most gains mustered on news of a debt upgrade Wednesday but recovered some ground late Thursday and were seen hard to call ahead of Friday's U.S. jobs report, dealers said.
"The debt upgrade showed the underlying trend of the market is firm, but we remain prey to the volatility on the international financial markets," said Jose Ignoto of brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 1.5 percent to close at 718.29.

The MerVal, which now shows a 3.0 percent loss on the week, had rallied 1.9 percent Wednesday after Standard & Poor's announced it was raising Argentina's long-term foreign currency debt rating to BB from BB-.

"We will get a mucher clearer picture of the near-term outlook tomorrow with the U.S. jobs report, which will show if inflationary pressures are indeed building up and warrant a credit tightening cycle," Napoli said.
Floor volume shrank to 13.8 million pesos from an already dismal tally of 16.8 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter deals rose to 72 million pesos from 59.3 million Wednesday.
The broad market index closed off 1.6 percent, with losers outstripping winners 39 to six and 12 issues closing flat.

All blue-chip stocks pulled back. The worst hit was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which dived 5.8 percent on buying by one institutional player forced to dump positions in futures contracts when his financing ran out, dealers said.
"In recent weeks Celulosa didn't post the recovery this buyer had hoped for and just continued to lag the rest of the market, mainly because of its dim earnings forecasts," one trader said.
The fall also took its toll on the oil sector, with YPF, Astra and Perez Companc, shedding 2.6 percent, 2.4 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively.
